Information since March points to a strong labor market and solid overall activity, but with Q1 softness in household spending and business investment and 12‑month inflation running below 2%. Holding the federal funds rate at 2.25–2.50% and signaling “patience” is consistent with Taylor‑rule and New Keynesian policy analyses (Taylor; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), which typically do not prescribe further tightening when inflation is below target and output is near potential. Low market‑based inflation compensation alongside stable survey expectations supports an inflation‑forecast‑targeting stance (Svensson and Woodford), reinforcing the cautious tone. Implementation via IOER at 2.35% to steer the funds rate within the corridor accords with the post‑2008 floor‑system framework (Goodfriend). Overall, the communication conveys cautiously positive growth with a dovish bias on inflation.
